description: Turns incoming MIDI into polyphonic pitch, gate and velocity, with eight assignable controller outputs and a full MPE mode

params.text: Steps the selected display field down by one
Steps the selected display field up by one
Holds notes on for as long as the sustain pedal controller is down, instead of ending them when the key is released
Chooses when the gate is dropped briefly to retrigger an envelope: on the first note of a phrase only, on every note, or on every note including those recovered from the held stack
Changes the value of whichever field is selected on the displays

outputs.text: The note pitch at 1V per octave, with transpose and the master pitch bend already folded in, one poly channel per voice
In the polyphonic modes, a second copy of the pitch offset by the random detune amount; in the MPE modes it carries the MPE Y axis controller instead
The per-note aftertouch of that voice in the polyphonic modes, and the MPE pressure axis in the MPE modes, 0V to 10V
The note-on velocity of that voice, 0V to 10V
The note-off velocity of that voice, 0V to 10V; in the MPE modes it can be switched to carry that voice's own pitch bend
10V while that voice is sounding, dropping for a millisecond when a note retriggers
The pitch bend of the master channel, -5V at the bottom of the wheel and +5V at the top, on one channel; the same bend is already applied to the pitch output
Whichever MIDI controller the display above it is set to, as 0V to 10V, smoothed

notes: Nothing comes out until a MIDI device is chosen: click the display at the top of the panel to pick a driver, a device and a channel
There is no right-click menu. Every setting is a field on the panel's displays: click one to select it, then turn the data knob or press the minus and plus buttons
Those fields cover the polyphony mode and voice count, the note and velocity ranges, the two pitch bend spans, detune, transpose, and which controller each of the eight outputs follows
A controller field can also learn: click it, then move a control on the MIDI device and the field takes that controller number
The pitch, second pitch, aftertouch, velocity, release velocity and gate jacks are poly cables whose channel count follows the voice setting; the other jacks are single channel
An Xpand module anywhere in the patch carries the voices above this module's own count, or a duplicate set of outputs, once the xpander field is set to its letter
